\paragraph{Pattern.}
The table shows a consistent pattern.  Items that were reverse-engineered
consistency requirements (colour completion; admissible EFT class) are
\emph{closed structurally} at the level that reverse analysis can
achieve.  Items that already had a forward Level~B/C route in
Parts~I--III (chirality, three generations, anomaly architecture,
matter representations, hypercharges, proton stability, neutrino
sector) are \emph{sharpened}: their precise formulation gains explicit
consistency constraints, but Part~IV does not turn them into
derivations.  Items that were implicit or ill-posed within ECT are
\emph{reframed}: they are now explicitly on the ledger.  Items with no
structural content addressable by reverse analysis (strong-sector
quantitative constants, confinement, glueball spectrum) remain
inherited from standard QCD phenomenology rather than derived.

\paragraph{Phenomenological interpretation of the admissible coupling
window.}
Beyond the qualitative status labels of the table, a phenomenological
reading of the admissible coupling window follows from the minimal EFT
of~\S\ref{sec:min_colour_eft} and from known experimental bounds.
The anisotropic channel~$\kappa_n^{\rm col}=Y_0/Z_0$ is strongly constrained and
is expected to be negligible in the infrared, consistent with the
structural argument relating~$Y(\phi)$ to the gravity-sector
anisotropy coefficient~$\alpha_{\rm ECT}$.  Large constant-background
departures of~$Z_0$ from unity are physically non-informative because
they are absorbed into matching-convention redefinitions at the
background level.  The topological background~$|\Theta(\bar\phi)|$ is
constrained by the neutron-electric-dipole bound to
$\lesssim 10^{-10}$; this is the sole precise phenomenological number
that enters the admissible window, and it drives the strong-CP
discussion of~\S\ref{sec:topological_strong_cp}.  For the matching
scale~$M_\ast$, structurally natural candidates within ECT are the
electroweak scale~$v_2$, the primary condensate scale
$\phi_0\sim M_{\rm Pl}$, or the condensate excitation scale; no
ECT-specific identification is established (O1 in
\S\ref{sec:part4_status}).  The combined picture is that, at
constant-background level, the admissible window is compatible with
standard QCD phenomenology but offers no independent predictive
leverage.  Predictive content requires dynamical $\phi$-dependence of
the coupling functions or an ECT-specific derivation of the matching
data, neither of which is supplied in the present minimal completion.

\paragraph{Bridging statement relative to existing open-status entries.}
Part~IV does not convert the existing open-status entries---such as
$N_{\rm gen}=3$, $\theta_{\rm QCD}$, flavour closure, and the
minimal-closure-hypothesis status of $N_{\rm colour}=3$---into derived
results.  What it does is sharpen the exact-colour completion layer on
which those entries depend, and separate what is now structurally
closed (the completion-layer existence, the admissible operator class,
the anomaly-consistency layer) from what remains genuinely unresolved
(the quantitative strong-sector constants, confinement, the glueball
spectrum, the strong-CP angle, and the full matter completion).  The
open-status entries retained in the status maps of the earlier parts
and in the quantitative-unification table~(\ref{tab:op_gut}) are
therefore not closed by Part~IV; they are reclassified within a
clearer architectural hierarchy.

\paragraph{What the table is not.}
The table is a bookkeeping device, not a results table.  No row
represents a new Level~A derivation.  Rows labelled ``Closed
structurally'' record only that the \emph{structural} consistency
question has been resolved at the reverse-analysis level; the
corresponding \emph{dynamical} questions (confinement, $\Lambda_{\rm QCD}$,
bound-state spectrum) remain on the Open list
of~\S\ref{sec:part4_status}.

% ============================================================
\section{Proton stability and baryon number as a UV discriminant}
\label{sec:proton_stability}
% ============================================================

\textit{Status: Level~C\@.  This subsection is conditional on the
unresolved gauge/flavour completion.}

\medskip
Proton stability is not part of the already established strict core
of ECT\@; it is a discriminant of how the presently open
gauge/flavour completion closes.
The proton lifetime answers a structural question: what low-energy
baryon-number selection rules are realised in the completed theory.
The detailed selection rules depend on the completed gauge/flavour
structure, an essential unresolved part of which is the colour
sector~(\S\ref{sec:colour_completion}).
Proton stability is therefore a conditional discussion-level result.

\subsubsection*{Three selection-rule patterns}

The completed theory may realise several distinct baryon-number
selection-rule patterns.

\paragraph{Pattern~I: full low-energy protection.}
The completed gauge/flavour sector enforces a selection rule
forbidding low-energy baryon-violating operators relevant for proton
decay and for the leading $\Delta B=2$ processes.
In this case no low-energy proton-decay channel is generated within
the completed effective theory.
In a gravitationally complete setting such protection is more
naturally realised through a gauged or discrete remnant than through
an exact continuous global~$U(1)_B$, in line with general
quantum-gravity arguments suggesting the absence of exact continuous
global symmetries~\cite{BanksSeiberg2011,HarlowOoguri2021}.

\paragraph{Pattern~II: partial protection.}
$\Delta B=1$ operators are forbidden, but $\Delta B=2$ transitions
remain allowed.
Proton decay is absent---not because baryon number is exactly
conserved, but because the completed low-energy selection rules
forbid precisely the $\Delta B=1$ channel.
More generally, the completed theory may preserve or violate
different combinations such as $B$, $L$, and $B-L$, which determine
the allowed operator classes.
In this pattern the relevant observational tests are
$n$--$\bar n$ oscillations and dinucleon decay rather than proton
decay.

\paragraph{Pattern~III: generic violation.}
If the completed field content below $\Lambda_B$ is
Standard-Model-like, no lighter baryon-violating mediators are
present, and the leading local $\Delta B=1$ operators are the usual
gauge-invariant dimension-six operators built from SM fields, then
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:proton_dim6}
  \mathcal{O}_B
  \;\sim\;
  \frac{C_B}{\Lambda_B^2}\,qqql.
\end{equation}
This is the natural leading EFT benchmark only under the specific
hypothesis that the spectrum below $\Lambda_B$ is
Standard-Model-like and that no lighter baryon-violating states
alter the operator hierarchy.
For the natural ECT ultraviolet scale
$\Lambda_B\sim\phi_0\sim\bar M_{\rm Pl}$
(in the present benchmark coinciding in order of magnitude with the
UV threshold of the ordered branch) the proton lifetime is
\begin{equation}
  \label{eq:proton_tau}
  \tau_p
  \;\sim\;
  \frac{\Lambda_B^4}{|C_B|^2\,m_p^5}
  \;\sim\;
  10^{41}\text{--}10^{42}\;\text{yr}
  \qquad(C_B=\mathcal{O}(1)).
\end{equation}
The structural ECT result is the three-pattern classification above.
The numerical lifetime $10^{41}$--$10^{42}\,$yr is the generic
EFT benchmark of Pattern~III, not an ECT-native derived decay
amplitude.

\subsubsection*{Connection to baryogenesis}

The present theory does not yet derive physical baryon number, a topological
baryogenesis bias, or an electroweak sphaleron operator: the relevant compact
bundle, chiral matter representations, violating vertex and state are missing.
Such operators may occur in a supplied completion, but their existence cannot
presently be used either to infer baryogenesis or to remove proton stability.
The completed low-energy baryon-number selection rules relevant for proton
decay remain Open.

Whether the same topological or sphaleron sector induces a local
$\Delta B=1$ nucleon-decay operator at zero temperature remains
open.
If it does, the present-day decay rate is controlled by a
zero-temperature Euclidean action (instanton/bounce-type suppression)
or by the induced effective operator, \emph{not} by thermal
Boltzmann suppression.

\subsubsection*{Experimental context and comparison}

The current Super-Kamiokande limit is
$\tau_p(p\to e^+\pi^0)>2.4\times10^{34}\,$yr~\cite{SuperK2020};
the expected sensitivity of
Hyper-Kamiokande~\cite{HyperK2018} is of order $10^{35}\,$yr.

Unlike conventional GUT models, ECT does not contain an intermediate
unification scale $\Lambda_{\rm GUT}\sim10^{16}\,$GeV\@.
In Pattern~III this pushes proton decay far beyond current and
foreseeable sensitivity.
In Patterns~I and~II the proton is stable.

Observation of $\Delta B=1$ proton decay in the
$10^{34}$--$10^{36}\,$yr window would exclude the proton-stable
branches (Patterns~I and~II) and strongly disfavour Pattern~III with
generic $C_B=\mathcal{O}(1)$.
Nucleon-decay searches thereby directly probe the ultraviolet status
of baryon number in ECT\@.

The specific branching pattern ($p\to e^+\pi^0$,
$p\to\bar\nu K^+$, etc.) is not fixed at the present stage, because
it depends on the detailed UV realisation of the gauge/flavour
sectors.

\paragraph{Status summary.}
This entire subsection is Level~C in the sense of
Table~\ref{tab:ect-levels}: it depends on the unresolved
gauge/flavour completion---especially the colour realisation---and on
baryon-number selection rules not yet derived from first principles.

\medskip\noindent
\textbf{Open problem (OP-proton).}
Derivation of baryon-number selection rules from the completed
gauge/flavour sector;
identification of which pattern (I/II/III) is realised;
if Pattern~III, identification of decay channels and coefficient
structure.


% ============================================================
\section{Topological sector and strong CP}
\label{sec:topological_strong_cp}
% ============================================================

\textit{Status: Level~C, Open.  Part~IV sharpens the
strong CP problem within ECT rather than solves it.}

\paragraph{The topological coupling is unavoidable.}
The operator $\Theta(\phi)\,F^a_{\mu\nu}\tilde F^{a\mu\nu}/(32\pi^2)$
in the minimal EFT~(eq.~\ref{eq:min_colour_eft}) is gauge-invariant
and compatible with all ECT symmetries.  No ECT postulate forbids it
at the Lagrangian level.

\paragraph{Reopening of strong CP.}
At constant macroscopic background $\phi=\bar\phi$, the effective theta parameter is
$\theta_{\rm eff}\equiv\Theta(\bar\phi)$.  The experimental bound from
the neutron electric dipole moment is
$|\theta_{\rm eff}|\lesssim 10^{-10}$.  Without a mechanism, the
natural expectation is $\theta_{\rm eff}=\mathcal{O}(1)$.  ECT with~P7
and the minimal EFT therefore reproduces the strong CP problem rather
than solving it.

\paragraph{Possible resolution routes, all currently Open.}

\emph{R1 --- CP-symmetric ordered branch.}\ \ Postulate that the
ordered condensate background respects CP as a residual symmetry,
forcing $\Theta(\bar\phi)\in\{0,\pi\}$.  This would require additional
structural input on the CP properties of the medium, which has not
been derived from the postulates P1--P7.

\emph{R2 --- axion-like relaxation.}\ \ Dynamical relaxation of
$\Theta(\phi)$ via a pseudoscalar mode with the required anomaly
coupling to $F\tilde F$.  The existing ordered-branch soft modes do
not presently supply a demonstrated axion-like degree of freedom: the
$O(4)\to O(3)$ Goldstones are scalars, not pseudoscalars, and do not
possess the required anomaly coupling.  Any axion-type resolution
would require additional pseudoscalar structure and an explicit
anomaly coupling, neither of which is available in the minimal P7
completion.

\emph{R3 --- geometric obstruction from $\Omega$.}\ \ The fixed
complex volume form in P7, together with appropriate CP-transformation
properties of $\mathcal{C}$, could in principle structurally force
$\Theta\equiv 0$.  R3 is conceptually attractive because it would
solve the problem without introducing a new low-energy field, but at
present no geometric derivation enforcing $\Theta\equiv 0$ is
available.

\paragraph{Witten--Veneziano consistency target.}
The $\eta'$ mass in QCD is related to the topological susceptibility
of the pure-gauge vacuum through the Witten--Veneziano relation
(Witten~1979; Veneziano~1979), schematically
\begin{equation}
m_{\eta'}^2 \,\approx\, \frac{4\,N_f}{f_\pi^2}\,\chi_{\rm top}^{\rm pure},
\end{equation}
where $\chi_{\rm top}^{\rm pure}$ is measured on the lattice for pure
$SU(3)$ at $\chi_{\rm top}^{1/4}\approx 198$~MeV.  Any ECT-specific
contribution through $\Theta(\phi)$ must preserve this infrared
relation, which provides a nontrivial consistency target: the product
of any ECT-induced topological coupling and the standard-QCD dynamical
content cannot shift the $\eta'$ mass outside its observed value.
This is the cleanest standard-QCD channel through which the
topological sector of the minimal P7 EFT can be matched to a measured
hadronic observable, and it reinforces that any $\Theta$-related
physics in ECT must be compatible with, rather than replace, the
standard Yang--Mills topological vacuum structure.

\paragraph{Final status.}
ECT with P7 and the minimal EFT does not solve the strong CP problem.
Accordingly, Part~IV sharpens the strong CP problem within ECT rather
than solving it.  Resolution is flagged for future work, with the
three routes above representing the currently identified lines of
attack.

% ============================================================
\section{ECT and the Yang--Mills mass-gap problem}
\label{sec:ect_yang_mills_gap}
% ============================================================

\textit{Status: the meta-statement on the Clay object
(Block~\ref{ymp:K2}) is a framework-definition conditional on P7, not a
derived physical theorem; the structural chain
$\mathrm{P7}\!\to\!SU(3)\!\to\!\mathrm{Tr}(F^2)$ is the Level~B result
of~\S\ref{sec:min_colour_eft}; the ECT-native gap statement is a
non-circular conditional theorem (Level~B/C); the residual is recorded
as two explicit open problems. Routine renormalisation-group algebra
and the numerical sensitivity table are collected in
Appendix~\ref{app:ym_rg_polymer}.}

This section addresses the Yang--Mills problem directly. Its purpose
is neither to claim a solution of the Clay Millennium problem nor to
dismiss it, but to separate the physical question from the
mathematical one, to establish which of the two ECT engages, and to
state precisely how far the engagement can presently be carried.

\subsection{Separation of the physical and mathematical questions}
\label{ymp:split}

The Clay formulation combines two logically independent statements,
and ECT must keep them apart; conflating them produces the spurious
dilemma of whether ECT ``solves'' the problem.

\emph{\textbf{(K1) The physical question.}} Why does the observed
strong sector exhibit confinement and a mass gap---no free,
arbitrarily soft coloured excitations, and quarks permanently bound
into colour-singlet states? This is a question about the real world.

\emph{\textbf{(K2) The mathematical question.}} Does a constructively
well-defined quantum \emph{pure} Yang--Mills theory exist on
$\mathbb{R}^4$ for a compact simple gauge group, with fundamental
Poincaré invariance and satisfying the Wightman or
Osterwalder--Schrader axioms, whose spectrum has a strictly positive
gap $\Delta>0$~\cite{JaffeWitten2000}? For $SU(3)$ this means glueball
states cannot be arbitrarily light. This is a question about a
specific mathematical object: the continuum measure of pure
Yang--Mills on flat $\mathbb{R}^4$.

The Clay prize is awarded for~(K2), the construction; it is
\emph{motivated} by~(K1), the physics. ECT relates differently to
each, and we treat them separately.

\subsection{Conditional P7 reformulation of the Clay object}
\label{ymp:K2}

\paragraph{Framework-definition statement (conditional on P7).}
\textit{The central object of~(K2)---fundamental, Poincaré-invariant,
continuum Yang--Mills on $\mathbb{R}^4$---is not a primitive object of
ECT. The Clay continuum object remains mathematically meaningful, but
it is not a fundamental referent of ECT: it appears only as a limiting
effective idealisation of the P7 colour sector.}

Given the P4/P7 ontology, three modelling choices motivate this
reformulation; they do not prove that the continuum Yang--Mills object is
absent from nature.

\emph{Lorentz invariance is a conditional completion target, not a
fundamental input.}  P4 supplies a Euclidean director.  In an independently
supplied scalar principal operator, the displayed coefficient inequality gives
a hyperbolic scalar classification; P5 does not own that result.  Exact
physical Poincaré invariance---a \emph{premise} of~(K2)---requires a separate
metric/clock and colour-sector action and remains Open for ECT.

\emph{The colour sector may be anisotropic.} The general colour EFT under
P7, eq.~(\ref{eq:min_colour_eft}), admits the operator
$Y(\phi)\,(n^\mu F^a_{\mu\rho})(n^\nu F_\nu^{\,a\rho})$, which contracts
the field strength with the same Lorentzian director $n^\mu$ that
enters the generalised Einstein equations of Part~II through the
anisotropy coefficient $\alpha_{\rm ECT}$. The colour sector of ECT is
therefore not pure isotropic Yang--Mills; it is Yang--Mills coupled to
an ordered medium with a preferred direction.

\emph{The exact-isotropy limit coincides with the decoupling limit.}
Pure isotropic continuum Yang--Mills is recovered only as
$Y\to 0$, $Z\to\text{const}$, $\Theta\to\text{const}$ with the
director dependence removed---precisely the UV-decoupling regime
of~\S\ref{sec:min_colour_eft} in which, by the background-level
triviality result, ECT returns \emph{standard} Yang--Mills with no
independent content. The only point at which the Clay object faithfully
describes the ECT colour sector is the degenerate point at which ECT
adds nothing beyond standard matching.

The careful statement is therefore not that the Clay object ``does not
exist''.  A Yang--Mills-like curvature term is standard mathematics after P7
and a local colour bundle/connection/action have been supplied; it is not
derived from P1--P6.  Its relation to a physical ECT colour sector and to the
fundamental continuum object of the Clay problem remains conditional/Open.

\subsection{The domain of applicability of the Clay problem, and where ECT lies}
\label{ymp:domain}

That the central object of~(K2) has no fundamental referent in ECT is
\emph{not a defect} of the Clay formulation. The problem is correctly
posed within its domain of applicability: fundamental quantum field
theory on a fixed Minkowski background. A problem posed about continuum
fields on $\mathbb{R}^4$ is not obliged to qualify its premises with
``provided spacetime is fundamental''---that is understood from its
context. ECT does not dispute~(K2) \emph{inside} this domain.

What the P7 completion proposes is that the realised strong sector lies
outside this fundamental-continuum description because spacetime and
Lorentz invariance are emergent.  This is a framework hypothesis, not an
empirical result established by the present action.
The situation is analogous to global energy conservation, which ceases
to hold on cosmological scales---not because the conservation law is
defective, but because a Friedmann--Robertson--Walker geometry has no
global timelike Killing vector and the law's premises are not met.
Likewise,~(K2) retains full validity within
fundamental-QFT-on-$\mathbb{R}^4$, while its central continuum object is
not a fundamental referent of ECT, because ECT describes a regime for
which the premise of a fundamental flat continuum does not hold.

This is the precise sense in which ECT \emph{reformulates} rather than
\emph{solves} or \emph{dismisses} the problem: it does not declare the
Clay question erroneous; it shows that the question is posed in an
idealisation whose central object is not primitive in the P7 definition, and it
transfers the physical content of~(K1) onto an object that \emph{is}
realised in the theory. This follows the same pattern by which ECT
treats other apparent paradoxes throughout this work---not by declaring
them false, but by exhibiting that they are framed in a non-fundamental
approximation.

\subsection{The ECT-native object and its reformulated question}
\label{ymp:native}

The P7 proposal does not merely remove the Clay object; it specifies a
candidate ECT object intended to carry the same physics and restates~(K1)
as a question about \emph{that} object. The replacements are:

\begin{itemize}
\item the \emph{fundamental continuum Yang--Mills measure on
  $\mathbb{R}^4$} is replaced by the \emph{compact non-Abelian $SU(3)$
  colour-frame sector of the $\Phi$-medium under~P7}, evaluated only
  below a supplied EFT breakdown scale $M_\ast$; a physical UV
  regulator or continuum completion is not derived;
\item the \emph{Clay spectral gap} is replaced by the \emph{finite
  correlation length $\xi_{\rm col}$} of all connected gauge-invariant
  colour-singlet correlators, with $\Delta_{\rm col}\gtrsim
  \xi_{\rm col}^{-1}$;
\item \emph{confinement as absence of coloured asymptotic states} is
  replaced by the \emph{finite-tension orientational
  flux-tube/holonomy response} of the medium between separated colour
  sources.
\end{itemize}

A crucial point on the \emph{scope} of the reformulated question.
The ECT-native task is a different finite-cutoff question from~(K2):
it asks for a gap at a supplied physical cutoff and does not establish
the continuum limit $a\to0$.  This may make a conditional polymer
analysis more tractable, but it is not logically equivalent to, stronger
than, or a solution of the Clay construction.  Calling the continuum
object non-primitive is an adopted P1--P7 framework definition, not an
empirical fact or mathematical theorem about nature.

Three separations are enforced throughout, on pain of confusion.
\emph{Pure-YM versus QCD-with-matter:} the \emph{pure} P7 colour
sector is the ECT analogue of the Clay pure-Yang--Mills object;
P7 \emph{plus} coloured matter is the analogue of full QCD;
confinement of dynamical quarks is a further, distinct physical
question and is not claimed here. \emph{CP-even versus
$\Theta\neq 0$:} the colour-gap statement is formulated first in the
CP-even sector $\theta_{\rm eff}=0$, where reflection positivity of the
gauge-invariant sector is cleanest; the extension to
$\Theta(\phi)\neq 0$ is entangled with the strong-CP problem
(\S\ref{sec:topological_strong_cp}) and is treated as a separate
problem. \emph{Zero-temperature vacuum:} the statement concerns the
zero-temperature vacuum colour sector; finite-temperature deconfinement
lies outside it. A note on continuum usage: ECT does not require a
\emph{fundamental} continuum limit $a\to 0$, but it freely uses
continuum fields as an \emph{effective infrared description}
---continuum-as-effective-IR yes, continuum-as-fundamental-all-scales
no.

\subsection{Renormalisation-group structure and the dynamical scale}
\label{ymp:rg}

No new postulate is introduced. In particular, a postulate of the form
``finite colour-orientational susceptibility'' is \emph{rejected}:
written as a quadratic coercivity
$\delta^2 S \ge \kappa\,\|a_{\rm phys}\|^2$ it would contradict
Theorem~1 of~\S\ref{sec:min_colour_eft} (transverse modes are
perturbatively massless) and would amount to a concealed gluon mass.
The gap is instead reached through the renormalisation-group structure
already present in~\S\ref{sec:min_colour_eft}.

The established structural chain is: P7 supplies a local $SU(3)$
colour-frame redundancy; locality and gauge invariance give the
connection $A_\mu$, the curvature $F_{\mu\nu}$, and the leading term
$\mathrm{Tr}(F^2)$; exactness of $SU(3)$ forbids a Proca gluon mass
(Theorem~1); the colour-singlet character of the $\Phi$-condensate
forbids a colour-Higgs route (Theorem~2); hence any physical gap must
be nonperturbative (Theorem~3). These are all in place.

The mechanism must respect asymptotic freedom, and a naive formulation
must be avoided: \emph{a strong-coupling expansion cannot be applied at
$M_\ast$}. For the structurally natural ECT candidates
$M_\ast\sim\phi_0\sim\bar M_{\rm Pl}$, asymptotic freedom makes
$g_s^2(M_\ast)$ \emph{small}, where strong-coupling methods
\emph{diverge}. The correct device is the two-scale structure already
implicit in eq.~(\ref{eq:Lambda_col_ECT}). The one-loop pure-$SU(3)$
$\beta$-function (matter-free; with $n_f$ quarks
$b_0 = 11 - 2n_f/3$, outside this pure-sector statement),
\begin{equation}
\mu\frac{dg}{d\mu} = -\frac{b_0\,g^3}{16\pi^2},\qquad b_0 = 11,
\label{eq:ym_beta}
\end{equation}
integrates to
\begin{equation}
\frac{1}{g^2(\mu)} = \frac{1}{g^2(M_\ast)}
+ \frac{b_0}{8\pi^2}\ln\frac{\mu}{M_\ast},
\qquad
g^2(\mu) = \frac{8\pi^2}{b_0\,\ln(\mu/\Lambda_{\rm col})},
\label{eq:ym_running}
\end{equation}
and generates, with the colour infrared scale of
eq.~(\ref{eq:Lambda_col_ECT}),
\begin{equation}
\Lambda_{\rm col}
= M_\ast \exp\!\left[-\frac{8\pi^2 Z_0}{b_0\,g_s^2(M_\ast)}\right],
\qquad
\mu_c = \Lambda_{\rm col}\,\exp\!\left[\frac{8\pi^2}{b_0\,x_c}\right],
\quad x \equiv \frac{g_s^2}{Z_0} = g_{\rm eff}^2,
\label{eq:ym_entry}
\end{equation}
where $\mu_c$ is the scale of entry into the strong-coupling region
for a chosen strong-coupling threshold $x_c$, and $x=g_{\rm eff}^2$ is
the canonically normalised effective coupling of~\S\ref{sec:min_colour_eft}.
Since $b_0=11>0$, the coupling \emph{necessarily} grows toward the
infrared, and dimensional transmutation generates a dynamical colour
scale exponentially below the threshold. Strong-coupling/cluster
methods are therefore applied after coarse-graining to
$a_{\rm col}\sim\Lambda_{\rm col}^{-1}$, not at $M_\ast$.
Only after the polymer endpoint theorem is invoked does one obtain
$\xi_{\rm col}=a_{\rm col}/m_{\rm lat}=O(a_{\rm col})$.

The inverse relation furnishes a matching condition,
\begin{equation}
\frac{g_s^2(M_\ast)}{Z_0}
= \frac{8\pi^2}{b_0\,\ln(M_\ast/\Lambda_{\rm col})},
\label{eq:ym_matching}
\end{equation}
whose numerical content and its exponential sensitivity to the
matching data are tabulated in Appendix~\ref{app:ym_rg_polymer}. Two
lessons follow. \emph{First}, at high $M_\ast$ the UV coupling is
genuinely weak, confirming that strong-coupling methods cannot act at
$M_\ast$---only after RG flow to $\Lambda_{\rm col}$. \emph{Second}, the
dependence is exponentially steep: at $M_\ast=\bar M_{\rm Pl}$ a shift
of $g_s^2/Z_0$ by $\pm 0.01$ moves $\Lambda_{\rm col}$ by roughly two
orders of magnitude. This is \emph{why} no numerical $\Lambda_{\rm col}$
is predicted: it would require $M_\ast$, $g_s(M_\ast)$, and $Z_0$ to be
derived rather than matched, and the exponential sensitivity amplifies
any uncertainty in them.

\subsection{The ECT-native gap theorem (non-circular, polymer-entry form)}
\label{ymp:theorem}

This is the technical core. It is formulated without introducing any
new postulate, and in a form that is non-circular by construction: the
hypotheses do not assume the decay one wishes to prove.

\begin{theorem}[ECT-native pure-colour mass gap, polymer-entry form]
\label{thm:ect_colour_gap}
Assume P1--P7, restricted to the zero-temperature, CP-even,
pure-colour P7 sector. Let $M_\ast$ be the physical ECT threshold and
let the pure-$SU(3)$ running of eq.~(\ref{eq:ym_running}) define the
dynamical scale $\Lambda_{\rm col}$ by eq.~(\ref{eq:ym_entry}). Suppose
that Wilsonian blocking to $a_{\rm col}\sim\Lambda_{\rm col}^{-1}$
produces a compact $SU(3)$ transfer-matrix-positive lattice action
whose character/polymer activities satisfy the polymer-convergence
bound stated below in eq.~(\ref{eq:ym_Q}). Then all connected
local gauge-invariant colour-singlet correlators decay exponentially,
\begin{equation}
\bigl|\langle\mathcal{O}(x)\,\mathcal{O}(0)\rangle_c\bigr|
\;\le\; C_{\mathcal{O}}\,e^{-m_{\rm lat}\,|x|/a_{\rm col}},
\qquad m_{\rm lat}>0,
\label{eq:ym_clustering}
\end{equation}
so that $\xi_{\rm col}=a_{\rm col}/m_{\rm lat}$, and the physical
pure-colour spectrum has a positive mass gap of the dynamically
generated scale,
\begin{equation}
\Delta_{\rm col}\;\ge\;\frac{m_{\rm lat}}{a_{\rm col}}
\;=\;C_{\rm gap}\,\Lambda_{\rm col}\;>\;0,
\qquad C_{\rm gap}=O(1),
\label{eq:ym_gap}
\end{equation}
with $C_{\rm gap}$ determined by the nonperturbative blocked action.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}[Proof (chain form)]
Under the hypotheses, the compact-$SU(3)$ strong-coupling cluster
(polymer) expansion converges
\cite{OsterwalderSeiler1978,Seiler1982}. The gap then follows as a
chain rather than from a single result:
\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
\text{polymer/cluster convergence}
&\;\Rightarrow\;
\text{exponential clustering},\\
\text{transfer-matrix positivity}
&\;\Rightarrow\;
\text{spectral representation}
\;\Rightarrow\;
\text{spectral gap.}
\end{aligned}
\nonumber
\end{equation}
Convergence of the expansion yields exponential clustering of
gauge-invariant correlators (eq.~\ref{eq:ym_clustering}) and, as a
confinement \emph{indicator}, an area law for Wilson loops with finite
string tension $\sigma>0$. Positivity of the transfer matrix at the
coarse-grained scale furnishes a physical Hilbert space with
self-adjoint $H\ge 0$ and the spectral representation
$C_{\mathcal{O}}(t)=\sum_n|\langle 0|\mathcal{O}|n\rangle|^2
e^{-(E_n-E_0)t}$. Since the clustering estimate is obtained for the local
gauge-invariant colour-singlet algebra, taken as a separating family of
physical observables, any physical state below $\xi_{\rm col}^{-1}$
would have nonzero overlap with some such operator and would produce a
slower exponential contribution in its Euclidean two-point function.
This contradicts the uniform exponential clustering bound. Therefore
no physical colour-singlet state lies in
$0<E_n-E_0<\xi_{\rm col}^{-1}$; with
$a_{\rm col}\sim\Lambda_{\rm col}^{-1}$ this gives
$\Delta_{\rm col}=C_{\rm gap}\Lambda_{\rm col}$.
\end{proof}

Several points fix the status and forestall misreadings.

\emph{Non-circular.} The hypothesis is ``the blocked activities satisfy
$Q(a_{\rm col})<Q_c$,'' \emph{not} ``the correlators decay.''
Exponential clustering is a \emph{consequence} of a standard
convergence theorem, not an assumption.

\emph{The decisive variable is the activity vector, not the coupling.}
A large $g_{\rm eff}$ does \emph{not} by itself imply small polymer
activities if the blocked action carries long loops, non-local tails,
mixed operators, $\theta$-phases, or anisotropic $Y$-terms. The
relevant strong-coupling variable is the character/polymer activity
vector of the blocked compact $SU(3)$ action, which controls
$g_{\rm eff}$ but is stronger than it.

\emph{Correct scale.} The endpoint is applied at
$a_{\rm col}\sim\Lambda_{\rm col}^{-1}$, giving
$\Delta_{\rm col}=C_{\rm gap}\Lambda_{\rm col}$; applying it instead at
$M_\ast^{-1}$ would give the physically absurd $\Delta\sim M_\ast$.

\emph{Gap via clustering, not via area law.} The mass gap is obtained
from exponential clustering plus transfer-matrix positivity; the area
law is cited as a confinement indicator, not as the bridge to the gap.

\emph{Scale convention.} $C_{\rm gap}$ is not $\approx 1$: in pure
$SU(3)$ the lightest glueball is several units of the chosen scale, so
$\Delta_{\rm col}=C_{\rm gap}\Lambda_{\rm col}$ with $C_{\rm gap}$
undetermined without nonperturbative matching. We do not write
$\Delta_{\rm col}\approx\Lambda_{\rm col}$.

\emph{Anisotropy is not the mechanism.} The operator
$Y(\phi)(n\!\cdot\!F)^2$ marks the difference from the Clay continuum
object (\S\ref{ymp:K2}); it is \emph{not} the gap mechanism, and must
be negligible or controlled under blocking in the colour vacuum sector,
lest the gap be bought at the price of broken Lorentz invariance.

\emph{Centre symmetry is a diagnostic, not the proof.} Unbroken
$\mathbb{Z}_3$ centre symmetry in the pure confining vacuum (vanishing
Polyakov loop) is a consistency condition, not the proof; the proof
runs through polymer convergence and the transfer matrix. With coloured
matter $\mathbb{Z}_3$ is explicitly broken---another reason to keep
pure-YM and QCD-with-matter separate.

The non-Abelian structure is where P7 earns its place: a confining
finite-correlation vacuum is natural for compact non-Abelian $SU(3)$,
whereas compact $U(1)$ admits a massless Coulomb phase. The naturalness
of hypothesis $Q(a_{\rm col})<Q_c$ rests on the sector being compact
non-Abelian $SU(3)$, not merely ``some gauge sector.''

\subsection{Precise localisation of the residual: the A/B/C split and the polymer-entry criterion}
\label{ymp:residual}

The hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:ect_colour_gap} dissect, in the ECT
setting, into a known external theorem plus two ECT-specific bridges.

\paragraph{Part~A --- endpoint theorem (known, external).}
For compact four-dimensional lattice $SU(3)$ in the appropriate
strong-coupling/polymer-convergence domain, standard constructive
lattice-gauge results establish area-law behaviour and exponential
clustering of gauge-invariant observables
\cite{OsterwalderSeiler1978,Seiler1982}; together with transfer-matrix
positivity this yields a positive spectral gap in the gauge-invariant
sector. This
is cited, not re-derived; crucially, Part~A applies only \emph{after}
polymer-entry is established.  The narrower finite-cutoff ECT question
does not include the Clay continuum construction, but this does
\emph{not} replace the proof that the blocked ECT action lies in the
convergence domain.

\paragraph{Why the ECT-native finite-cutoff question is narrower.}
What makes~(K2) hard is \emph{not} the existence of a confining basin
---it exists at strong coupling---but the survival of the gap through
the \emph{continuum limit} $a\to 0$, where asymptotic freedom drives
the coupling to zero. \emph{In ECT there is no continuum limit
$a\to 0$:} the ordered branch carries a physical threshold $M_\ast$,
hence a physical floor $a_{\rm col}\gtrsim M_\ast^{-1}$.  The continuum
requirement is absent from the adopted ECT-native question by definition.
That narrows the question but does not make progress on the Clay continuum
construction and does \emph{not} by itself prove the gap, because
at fixed cutoff distinct phases remain possible; finiteness of the
cutoff alone does not forbid a massless phase. What remains is to show
that the \emph{physical} P7 branch lies in the convergence domain,
which is the content of Parts~B and~C.

\paragraph{Part~B --- RG-entry (ECT-specific).}
This splits in two. \emph{B1}: the coupling grows in the infrared and
$\Lambda_{\rm col}$ is generated---\emph{derived perturbatively} from
$b_0=11>0$ via eqs.~(\ref{eq:ym_running})--(\ref{eq:ym_entry}).
\emph{B2}: the flow actually enters the convergence domain with no
intermediate Coulomb/deconfined fixed point \emph{along the ECT
trajectory}---\emph{not rigorously proven}. B2 is a trajectory
statement, not the global claim that ``$SU(3)$ has no Coulomb phase for
all $\beta$.''

\paragraph{Part~C --- class-preservation (ECT-specific, open).}
Even granting that the strong-coupling domain is reached, one must show
that the blocked action at $a_{\rm col}$ remains in the local
(or exponentially local), compact, transfer-matrix-positive class to
which the endpoint theorem applies. Blocking from $M_\ast$ to
$a_{\rm col}$ may generate rectangular and chair loops, multi-plaquette
interactions, long-range tails, anisotropic $n\!\cdot\!F$ terms,
$\theta$-dependent phases, matter-induced centre breaking, or loss of
transfer positivity, any of which would take the system outside the
theorem's class. This is not automatic.

\paragraph{The residual as a checkable criterion.}
Rather than an abstract ``the sector enters the confining basin,'' the
conjunction B2$\,\wedge\,$C is made concrete. Expand the blocked
compact-$SU(3)$ action in $SU(3)$ characters,
\begin{equation}
e^{-S_{\rm eff}(U)}
= \prod_p\Bigl[\,1+\sum_{R\neq 0} c_R(a_{\rm col})\,\chi_R(U_p)\Bigr]
\times e^{-S_{\rm poly}^{\rm nonplaq}(U)},
\label{eq:ym_character}
\end{equation}
where $R$ runs over nontrivial irreducible representations, $\chi_R$
are the characters, and $c_R$ the activities. For a Wilson-type seed
$S_W=-(\beta_{\rm eff}/3)\sum_p\mathrm{Re}\,\mathrm{Tr}\,U_p$ at small
$\beta_{\rm eff}$ the leading activities are
$c_{\mathbf 3}=c_{\bar{\mathbf 3}}=\beta_{\rm eff}/6+O(\beta_{\rm eff}^2)$,
with higher representations of order $O(\beta_{\rm eff}^2)$. The polymer
expansion converges if
\begin{equation}
Q(a_{\rm col}) :=
\sum_{R\neq 0} d_R\,|c_R(a_{\rm col})|\,e^{\alpha\,C_2(R)}
+ \bigl\|S_{\rm poly}^{\rm nonplaq}(a_{\rm col})\bigr\|_\alpha
\;<\; Q_c\bigl(d{=}4,\,SU(3)\bigr),
\label{eq:ym_Q}
\end{equation}
with $d_R$ the dimension of $R$, $C_2(R)$ its quadratic Casimir,
$\alpha$ a norm parameter, and $Q_c$ the convergence-domain constant.
Convergence implies exponential clustering, hence finite
$\xi_{\rm col}$, hence $\Delta_{\rm col}=C_{\rm gap}\Lambda_{\rm col}$.
The bound $Q(a_{\rm col})<Q_c$ is the precise nonperturbative
replacement, in ECT, for the informal phrase ``the colour sector enters
the confining basin.''

The residual splits into two sharply scoped open problems.

\begin{description}
\item[\textnormal{\textbf{(OP-YM-polymer-entry-I --- class/positivity).}}]
Show that ECT Wilsonian blocking from $M_\ast$ to $a_{\rm col}$
preserves compact $SU(3)$ link variables, locality (or exponential
locality), and transfer-matrix positivity in the pure CP-even sector.
\item[\textnormal{\textbf{(OP-YM-polymer-entry-II --- activity bound).}}]
Show that the blocked character/polymer activities satisfy
$Q(a_{\rm col})<Q_c$, eq.~(\ref{eq:ym_Q})---equivalently, bound the
blocked action in a polymer norm relative to the compact-$SU(3)$ Wilson
strong-coupling action,
$\|S_{\rm eff}(a_{\rm col})-S_{\rm Wilson}^{\rm strong}\|_{\rm polymer}
<\varepsilon_c$.
\end{description}

With Part~A, OP-YM-polymer-entry-I and~II together imply the
ECT-native colour gap. The scope is precisely delimited: Part~A is an
external endpoint theorem applicable once polymer-entry has been
established.  The adopted finite-cutoff question simply does not include
the additional Clay requirement that the gap survive a fundamental
$a\to0$ limit.  B1 is derived from $b_0>0$; only B2 (trajectory entry) and~C
(class preservation under blocking) remain, now phrased as the two
concrete bounds~I and~II---checkable mathematical tasks, not a
philosophical gap.

\paragraph{Clay-upgrade criterion.}
If, in addition, the ECT colour sector admitted a formal continuum
limit $a\to 0$ preserving Osterwalder--Schrader/Wightman positivity
with $\Delta_{\rm col}\to\Delta>0$, then the ECT-native result would
upgrade to a solution of~(K2). ECT does \emph{not} claim this, and---by
\S\ref{ymp:K2}---its ontology does not require this limit to be
fundamental. The continuum limit is the bridge to the Clay prize; ECT
regards it as a mathematical idealisation external to its own physical
content.

\paragraph{The true bottleneck.}
The numerical value of $\xi_{\rm col}$ (equivalently $\Lambda_{\rm col}$,
and the constant $C_{\rm gap}$) is not derivable as long as $M_\ast$,
$g_s(M_\ast)$, and $Z_0$ remain matching data rather than ECT-derived
quantities; the exponential sensitivity of
eq.~(\ref{eq:ym_matching}) (Appendix~\ref{app:ym_rg_polymer}) makes
this acute. These would become calculable if the zero-mode derivation
of~P7 were achieved---i.e.\ if $\mathcal{C}_x\simeq\ker
\mathcal{D}_{\rm defect}$ with $\dim_{\mathbb{C}}=3$ were established,
fixing the internal module and its couplings from condensate dynamics.
We emphasise, however, that this would \emph{deepen the origin} of the
colour sector and make the gap \emph{quantitative}; it is \emph{not a
prerequisite} for the logical formulation of the colour-gap programme.
P7 is a full ECT postulate of the same standing as P1--P6, and the
programme is correctly posed \emph{given}~P7. The zero-mode derivation
is the route to a quantitative gap, not a precondition for the
existence statement.

\paragraph{Summary of the engagement.}
ECT does not solve the Clay problem~(K2) in its literal form and does
not dismiss it.  By adopted P1--P7 framework definition, it treats the
central object of~(K2) as non-primitive and proposes a different
finite-cutoff question for the correlation length $\xi_{\rm col}$ of
the supplied compact P7 $SU(3)$ colour-frame sector.  This is neither a
Level-A theorem nor a claim of superior physical relevance.  From P7 the
Yang--Mills structure and the exclusion of
all perturbative mass routes follow; the pure-$SU(3)$ running with
$b_0=11$ generates $\Lambda_{\rm col}$; and the ECT-native gap
$\Delta_{\rm col}=C_{\rm gap}\Lambda_{\rm col}$ follows from the
non-circular conditional Theorem~\ref{thm:ect_colour_gap}. The remaining residual has been sharpened below into a heat-kernel/HKLoc
entry criterion: OP-YM-polymer-entry-I and the combinatorial part of
OP-YM-polymer-entry-II reduce, in the chosen blocking framework, to one
explicit one-sided matching premise for the anisotropy parameter
$\zeta_Y(a_{\rm col})$, eq.~\eqref{eq:hk_ybudget}; in the
delayed-entry existence form, eq.~\eqref{eq:hk_ybudget_blocks}, this
premise is satisfied by any finite $O(1)$-bounded $\zeta_Y^{(n)}$
with $1+\zeta_Y^{(n)}>0$. This is far
narrower than the Clay problem, but it remains a conditional finite-cutoff
entry statement rather than an unconditional colour-gap proof.

\paragraph{A sharpened heat-kernel entry criterion (Level~B / conditional
reduction).}
\textit{Status: Level~B conditional reduction within a fixed
heat-kernel/local-cumulant blocking framework; not a Clay--Yang--Mills
construction and not a proof of the colour gap.}
Standard heat-kernel and one-loop conventions used in this bookkeeping follow
the background-field/heat-kernel literature~\cite{DeWitt1965,Gilkey1995,Vassilevich2003};
those references do not supply the ECT matching premise below.
The following heat-kernel coarse-graining analysis sharpens the residual pair
OP-YM-polymer-entry-I/II into a single explicitly named input. Working
with a canonical $b=2$ planar fusion of each coarse plaquette, one finds
that the pure same-plane heat-kernel sector integrates exactly to the
coarse-plaquette kernel $K_{4s}$, so same-plane ``staple'' strips are
intermediate fusion objects rather than independent polymer remainders;
the genuine non-core remainder is carried by cross-plane connected
cumulants, higher multi-leg cumulants, and the ECT-specific anisotropic
$Y$-terms. For the zero-singlet cross-plane sector, Peter--Weyl spectral
contraction of the heat-kernel smoothing supplies an $e^{-8s}$ envelope
for the leading two-leg non-singlet cumulants. As derived below, in a natural
local cumulant norm the leading bookkeeping estimate takes the form $K_{\rm
cross}\le 96\,C_{\rm loc}$, with $C_{\rm loc}$ fixed by the locality and
Casimir weights, so that $K_{\rm cross}\,e^{-8s}<1$ already for $s\gtrsim
0.75$; higher cumulants contract faster, and in $d=4$ the leading
single-link $m\ge 3$ source carries no third independent transverse
direction and reduces, after core subtraction, to the controlled
two-leg sector. Within this framework the positivity/reflection-positivity
and class-preservation content of OP-YM-polymer-entry-I, together with the
combinatorial part of the activity bound OP-YM-polymer-entry-II, are
reduced to a finite local norm-bookkeeping lemma. The \emph{single}
remaining genuinely ECT-specific input is then a \emph{leg-resolved}
budget for the anisotropy operator $Y(\phi)(n\!\cdot\!F)^2$ of
\S\ref{sec:min_colour_eft}; part~(v) of the derivation below shows that
its dangerous one-leg polymer channel is absent after extraction of the
plane-resolved anisotropic core, leaving a single explicit one-sided
matching inequality for the softening anisotropy $\zeta_Y(a_{\rm col})$. We stress the scope: this is a sufficient
heat-kernel \emph{entry} criterion conditional on the $Y$-budget and on
the chosen blocking framework, sharpening---but not closing---the colour
polymer-entry problem, and making no claim about a continuum
Yang--Mills construction.

\paragraph{Derivation of the heat-kernel bookkeeping reduction.}
We record the finite calculation behind the preceding criterion, since it
is part of the ECT-native polymer-entry problem rather than an external
Clay--continuum construction. Throughout, $s>0$ denotes the heat-kernel
smoothing time of one blocking step, and
\begin{equation}
K_s(U)=\sum_R d_R\,e^{-sC_2(R)}\chi_R(U)
\label{eq:hk_central_kernel}
\end{equation}
is the central heat kernel on $SU(3)$, with $d_R$ the dimension,
$\chi_R$ the character, and $C_2(R)$ the quadratic Casimir of the
irreducible representation $R$; the fundamental value is
$C_F\equiv C_2(\mathbf{3})=4/3$ and the adjoint value
$C_2(\mathbf{8})=3$.

\emph{(i) Canonical planar fusion.} The kernels~\eqref{eq:hk_central_kernel}
form a convolution semigroup,
\begin{equation}
\int dV\,K_s(UV^{-1})\,K_t(VW^{-1})=K_{s+t}(UW^{-1}),
\label{eq:hk_convolution}
\end{equation}
which follows termwise from the orthogonality relation
$\int dV\,\chi_R(UV^{-1})\chi_{R'}(VW^{-1})
=\delta_{RR'}\,\chi_R(UW^{-1})/d_R$. Iterating
eq.~\eqref{eq:hk_convolution}, a $2\times2$ same-plane heat-kernel block
fuses exactly to the coarse-plaquette kernel,
\begin{equation}
K_s^{*4}=K_{4s}.
\label{eq:hk_fourfold}
\end{equation}
Hence same-plane strips $K_{2s}$ are intermediate objects in a canonical
planar fusion tree; they are not independent polymer remainders. Distinct
row/column fusion trees yield the same $K_{4s}$ by associativity and
commutativity of~\eqref{eq:hk_convolution}, so the choice of a canonical
tree is a bookkeeping convention that avoids double-counting, not a
physical anisotropy. With this convention the same-plane staple remainder
vanishes identically, $R_{\rm staple}=0$. Moreover, each $K_s$ is a
strictly positive central class function, and the canonical fusion acts
by positive convolution (Markov) kernels compatible with link
reflection; reflection positivity of the blocked measure is therefore
preserved at every blocking step~\cite{OsterwalderSeiler1978,Seiler1982}.

\emph{(ii) Cross-plane spectral contraction.} The genuine non-core source
at this order is the cross-plane attachment sector. In a $b=2$, $d=4$
block the $2\times2$ coarse plaquette has four interior links, and at each
such link there are four genuine cross-plane attachment pairs, so the
combinatorial multiplicity is
\begin{equation}
N_{\rm cross}=4\cdot4=16
\label{eq:hk_ceff}
\end{equation}
(four interior links $\times$ four cross-plane attachment pairs per
link, the latter being two directions transverse to the fixed
coarse-plaquette plane times two orientations). The
heat-kernel smoothing acts as the Peter--Weyl operator, diagonal on
representation blocks,
\begin{equation}
T_t\,f_R=e^{-tC_2(R)}\,f_R .
\label{eq:hk_peterweyl}
\end{equation}
Since the planar block advances $s\mapsto4s$, the additional smoothing
carried by each non-trivial leg is $\Delta s=3s$. A leading cross
cumulant has two fundamental non-singlet legs; after singlet (and
normalisation) subtraction its spectral envelope is therefore
\begin{equation}
\exp\!\bigl[-2\,(3s)\,C_F\bigr]
=\exp\!\bigl[-2\,(3s)\,\tfrac{4}{3}\bigr]
=e^{-8s},
\label{eq:hk_eight}
\end{equation}
which is the origin of the $e^{-8s}$ contraction. A one-leg remainder, if
present, would contract only as $e^{-4s}$; this is precisely why the
anisotropic $Y$-sector must be budgeted separately. That no non-trivial
leg can integrate to a constant (which would escape the
contraction~\eqref{eq:hk_eight}) follows from Haar orthogonality: a single
fundamental leg has vanishing Haar average, so a local connected cumulant
cannot shed a leg into the singlet without an explicit subtraction.

\emph{(iii) Local cumulant norm and the constant $96$.} For definiteness,
control the remainders in a local connected-cumulant norm
\begin{equation}
\|R\|_{\rm HKLoc}
=\sup_X\,e^{L\,{\rm diam}(X)}
\sum_\lambda |r_X(\lambda)|
\Bigl(\textstyle\prod_{\ell} d_{\lambda_\ell}^{\,p}\Bigr)
\exp\!\Bigl[\alpha\textstyle\sum_\ell C_2(\lambda_\ell)\Bigr],
\label{eq:hkloc_norm}
\end{equation}
with the soft choice $p=1$ and moderate $\alpha,L\in[\tfrac14,\tfrac12]$;
here $X$ ranges over connected link supports, $\lambda$ over the
representation labels on their legs, and $r_X(\lambda)$ are the cumulant
coefficients. Under the canonical $b=2$ projection $\pi$ the diameter
contracts,
\begin{equation}
{\rm diam}(\pi(X))\le\bigl\lceil{\rm diam}(X)/2\bigr\rceil
\le \tfrac12\,{\rm diam}(X)+\tfrac12,
\label{eq:hk_diam}
\end{equation}
which is the integer identity
$|\lfloor u/2\rfloor-\lfloor v/2\rfloor|\le\lceil|u-v|/2\rceil$ applied
coordinatewise (the additive constant sharpens to $1/2$ for
site-projected supports and is bounded by $1$ with link/plaquette
thickening). The local projection multiplicity of a leading cross source
is one in the canonical fusion convention, $\mu_{\rm proj}=1$, while the
coarse-plaquette valence supplies the finite bound
$\mu_{\rm loc}\le 2(d-1)=6$. Collecting~\eqref{eq:hk_ceff}, the valence,
and the norm weights, the leading cross constant obeys
\begin{equation}
K_{\rm cross}\le N_{\rm cross}\cdot\mu_{\rm loc}\cdot C_{\rm loc}(\alpha,L)
=16\cdot6\cdot C_{\rm loc}(\alpha,L)
=96\,C_{\rm loc}(\alpha,L),
\label{eq:hk_96}
\end{equation}
where $C_{\rm loc}$ collects the harmless diameter and Casimir-margin
factors, schematically $C_{\rm loc}\sim e^{L}\,e^{\alpha/3}$ (the exponent
$\alpha/3$ being the Casimir difference
$C_2(\mathbf{8})-2C_2(\mathbf{3})=1/3$), and remains below $4$ over the
moderate parameter range used here. Hence
\begin{equation}
K_{\rm cross}\,e^{-8s}<1
\qquad\text{for}\qquad
s\gtrsim 0.75,
\label{eq:hk_threshold}
\end{equation}
since $\ln(96\,C_{\rm loc})/8<0.75$ for all $C_{\rm loc}\le4$.

\emph{(iv) Higher cumulants and the $m\ge3$ sector.} The
adjoint-promotion branch carries a larger dimension factor but a stronger
spectral suppression and is subdominant in the $p=1$ norm for
$s\gtrsim0.75$. Higher multi-leg cumulants carry at least the $e^{-12s}$
envelope. The only delicate case is a leading single-internal-link triple:
relative to the fixed coarse-plaquette plane there are only $d-2=2$
transverse directions in $d=4$, so the ordered triples of
\emph{distinct} cross-plane directions number $(d-2)(d-3)(d-4)=0$ and
no source supported on a single internal link probes three independent
cross-plane directions. Every such $m=3$
configuration therefore contains a same-plane subpair and reduces, after
canonical core subtraction, to the already controlled $\le2$-leg sector.
Multi-internal-link higher cumulants are treated as higher-support HKLoc
remainders: they acquire the same spectral suppression
of~\eqref{eq:hk_peterweyl} together with the diameter/locality weight
of~\eqref{eq:hkloc_norm}, and are bounded by the same estimates rather
than claimed to vanish.

\emph{(v) The anisotropy operator and the leg-resolved $Y$-budget.} The
remaining input is the anisotropy operator $Y(\phi)(n\!\cdot\!F)^2$
of~\S\ref{sec:min_colour_eft}. Its structural reduction rests on the fact
that the director $n$ and the coefficient $Y(\phi)$ carry no colour
indices: every single-plaquette contribution of the operator is a
$c$-number weight multiplying a gauge-invariant function of that one
plaquette, hence a class function, and the deformed weight remains
central to all orders in the field strength. At leading matching order
the deformation is an orientation-dependent rescaling of the heat-kernel
time, $s_t=s/(1+\zeta_Y)$ on plaquettes containing the $n$-direction and
$s_\sigma=s$ on the transverse ones, with $\zeta_Y$ denoting the dimensionless plane-resolved
heat-kernel anisotropy (in the minimal colour EFT normalisation,
$\zeta_Y$ is proportional to $\kappa_n^{\rm col}=Y_0/Z_0$, with
scheme constants absorbed into its definition at the entry scale).
Equivalently, in the character expansion the first-order deformation is
a Casimir-weighted central tower; in the entry window
$s>3\ln 3/5\simeq0.659$ the fundamental $3\oplus\bar 3$ branch is the
leading non-trivial label, so the leading-label bookkeeping is the same
as in the isotropic cross-sector estimate of part~(iii). The canonical
fusion of part~(i) acts within a single plane class and
holds verbatim, $K_{s_p}^{*4}=K_{4s_p}$ plane by plane; pointwise
positivity and the transfer/reflection structure compatible with the
director $n$ persist for all $s_t,s_\sigma>0$ (no claim of restored
hypercubic reflection symmetry is made). Two facts then empty the
dangerous channel. First, a parity lemma of the $b=2$ skeleton:
\emph{no closed loop carries exactly one integrated (non-skeleton)
link}. Skeleton sites have at most one odd coordinate; both endpoints of
the unique non-skeleton link $(z,\rho)$ would have to be skeleton sites,
forcing the odd coordinate $\nu\neq\rho$ of $z$ to be unique and
$z_\rho$ to be even, so that $z+\hat\rho$ acquires two odd
coordinates---a contradiction. (An exhaustive check on a $4^4$ patch
gives the plaquette skeleton-link distribution
$\{0{:}1152,\ 1{:}0,\ 2{:}384\}$ and no loop with a single integrated
link.) Second, Haar orthogonality as in part~(ii) annihilates any
hypothetical single non-trivial label on an integrated link. Hence,
after extraction of the plane-resolved anisotropic core $K_{4s_p}$, the
one-leg polymer remainder vanishes at single-plaquette order,
$R^{\rm polymer}_{Y,\rm 1leg}=0$; gradients of $n$ and $Y$ and
multi-plaquette composites are higher-support remainders in the sense of
part~(iv). The surviving two-leg envelopes are plane-resolved,
$e^{-4s_a-4s_b}\le e^{-8s_{\min}}$ with
$s_{\min}=s/(1+\max(0,\zeta_Y))$, so the bookkeeping
of~\eqref{eq:hk_96}--\eqref{eq:hk_threshold} yields the single one-sided
matching premise
\begin{equation}
\max\bigl(0,\zeta_Y(a_{\rm col})\bigr)\;\le\;
\frac{s}{s_{\rm entry}(C_{\rm loc})}-1,
\qquad
1+\zeta_Y(a_{\rm col})>0,
\label{eq:hk_ybudget}
\end{equation}
with $s_{\rm entry}(C_{\rm loc})\equiv\ln(96\,C_{\rm loc})/8$ the
threshold of~\eqref{eq:hk_threshold}. Numerically this is a softening
budget of $+0.53$ ($+0.34$) at $s=1$ for $C_{\rm loc}\le1.95$
($C_{\rm loc}\le4$); it is robust across the entry window for the soft
norm estimate, while the conservative $C_{\rm loc}=4$ requires
$s\gtrsim0.9$ or a very small positive $\zeta_Y$. The tightness of this conservative corner is, however, an artefact of
reading eq.~\eqref{eq:hk_ybudget} at the earliest admissible entry
scale. Because the plane-resolved heat-kernel core is stable under
the same $b=2$ convolution, $K_{s_p}^{*4}=K_{4s_p}$, the core
anisotropy ratio is unchanged by this blocking while the available
smoothing time grows as $s\mapsto4s$ per step. The HKLoc remainders
are transported through the additional block by the same finite local
bookkeeping as parts~(ii)--(iv), under the
small-remainder/stability-ball hypothesis already contained in
OP-YM-polymer-entry-II. Thus the $Y$-budget may be read as an
existence criterion over the blocking depth:
\begin{equation}
\exists\,n\ge0:\qquad
\max\bigl(0,\zeta_Y^{(n)}\bigr)\;\le\;
\frac{4^{\,n}s}{s_{\rm entry}(C_{\rm loc})}-1,
\qquad
1+\zeta_Y^{(n)}>0,
\label{eq:hk_ybudget_blocks}
\end{equation}
where $\zeta_Y^{(n)}$ denotes the plane-resolved anisotropy after
$n$ compatible $b=2$ blocking steps; for the pure heat-kernel core
$\zeta_Y^{(n)}=\zeta_Y(a_{\rm col})$, while the non-core
corrections are controlled by the HKLoc stability bound. The pure
cross-sector condition $K_{\rm cross}\,e^{-8\cdot4^{n}s}<1$ is
monotone in $n$ and is automatic at later blocks once it holds at the
earliest one. One additional block raises the conservative budget
from $+0.008$ to $+3.03$ at $(s,C_{\rm loc})=(0.75,4)$. Hence the
delayed-entry criterion covers the expected small or order-unity
softening anisotropies with finite blocking depth; choosing a later
entry block changes only the nonuniversal $O(1)$ gap constant
$C_{\rm gap}$ in eq.~\eqref{eq:ym_gap}. Negative $\zeta_Y$
strengthens the contraction and consumes no budget beyond
$1+\zeta_Y>0$. The value $\zeta_Y(a_{\rm col})$ itself is matching data
at the same level as $M_*$, $g_s(M_*)$ and $Z_0$, deferred to the
zero-mode matching programme; the $Y$-sector is thus structurally
benign, and the entry criterion holds conditionally on the one-sided
budget, read either in the earliest-entry form~\eqref{eq:hk_ybudget}
or in the delayed-entry form~\eqref{eq:hk_ybudget_blocks}.

\emph{Consequence.} Within this fixed heat-kernel/HKLoc blocking
framework, the same-plane sector~\eqref{eq:hk_fourfold}, the cross-sector
bookkeeping~\eqref{eq:hk_96}--\eqref{eq:hk_threshold}, the
reflection-positive iterability of the blocking, and the higher-cumulant
estimates together reduce the positivity/class-preservation content of
OP-YM-polymer-entry-I and the combinatorial part of the activity bound
OP-YM-polymer-entry-II to one remaining ECT-specific input, whose structure part~(v) resolves:
the one-leg polymer channel of the anisotropy operator
$Y(\phi)(n\!\cdot\!F)^2$ of~\S\ref{sec:min_colour_eft} is absent after
extraction of the plane-resolved anisotropic core, and what remains is
the single one-sided matching inequality~\eqref{eq:hk_ybudget} for the
softening anisotropy $\zeta_Y(a_{\rm col})$, whose value is zero-mode
matching data. Equivalently, in the delayed-entry form~\eqref{eq:hk_ybudget_blocks},
this matching requirement becomes an existence-over-blocks condition
for the bounded anisotropy $\zeta_Y^{(n)}$. The earliest-entry
($n=0$) reading remains a useful sharpening tied to the detailed P7
matching value, but it is not required for the Level~B delayed-entry
sufficient criterion. This is a Level~B finite-bookkeeping
reduction within the chosen framework---not a continuum Yang--Mills
construction and not a proof of the colour gap. The full version history
of the reduction, including the intermediate corrections, is kept in the
author's supplementary derivation notes.

\paragraph{Three distinct questions in the strong sector.}
It is useful to keep three structurally different questions apart,
because ECT with~P7 has different status with respect to each.
(i)~\emph{Existence of a colour infrared scale.} The admissible EFT
of~\S\ref{sec:min_colour_eft} is consistent with a nonzero infrared
scale $\Lambda_{\rm col}$, inherited from standard QCD phenomenology;
ECT does not derive its value but constrains how medium couplings may
affect it.
(ii)~\emph{Existence of a gauge-invariant mass gap in the exact colour
sector.} This is a physically sharper statement than~(i): no
gauge-invariant physical state below a finite threshold.  In the
ECT-native formulation this question is addressed by the conditional
polymer-entry theorem of~\S\ref{sec:ect_yang_mills_gap}: if the blocked
pure P7 colour sector lies in the compact transfer-positive
polymer-convergence domain, then a positive gap
$\Delta_{\rm col}=C_{\rm gap}\Lambda_{\rm col}$ follows.  This is not an
unconditional derivation; after the heat-kernel/HKLoc reduction of
\S\ref{sec:ect_yang_mills_gap}, the remaining explicit premise is the
one-sided matching estimate~\eqref{eq:hk_ybudget} for
$\zeta_Y(a_{\rm col})$; in its delayed-entry existence
form~\eqref{eq:hk_ybudget_blocks} it is satisfied by any finite
$O(1)$-bounded $\zeta_Y$ with $1+\zeta_Y>0$, so the exact matching
value enters only the earliest-entry sharpening.
(iii)~\emph{Full derivation of the glueball spectrum.} This is a
quantitative dynamical question inaccessible from structural reverse
analysis.
The Clay Millennium formulation of the Yang--Mills existence-and-mass-gap
problem~\cite{JaffeWitten2000} is distinct again: it requires
constructive quantum field theory on $\mathbb{R}^4$ with fundamental
Poincaré invariance and Wightman or Osterwalder--Schrader axioms.
ECT with~P7 proceeds in a different setting---a colour sector coupled
to an ordered condensate medium, with Lorentz invariance emergent
rather than fundamental. The relationship between ECT and the Clay
problem is therefore not one of solution or contact in the latter's
stated form, but of reformulation: \S\ref{sec:ect_yang_mills_gap}
separates the physical question~(K1) from the mathematical question~(K2),
records, by the adopted P1--P7 framework definition, that the Clay
continuum object is not primitive in this model; this is neither a derived
physical theorem nor a solution/dismissal of the Clay problem.  It transfers
the conditional analogue of~(K1) onto the finite correlation length
of the compact P7 colour-frame sector, where a non-circular conditional
mass-gap theorem is available.

\paragraph{Final note on claims level.}
Framework-definition statements such as the non-primitive status assigned
to the Clay continuum object in~\S\ref{sec:ect_yang_mills_gap} are adopted
ontology under P1--P7, not Level-A physical theorems.  The constructive and
quantitative claims of Part~IV remain Level~B or~C/Open.
Quantitative strong-sector observables
($\Lambda_{\rm QCD}$, confinement, glueball masses) remain inherited
from standard Yang--Mills and QCD phenomenology, constrained by the
admissible EFT structure of~\S\ref{sec:min_colour_eft} but not
independently derived.

\section{Synthesis of Part~IV}
\label{sec:part4_synthesis}
% ============================================================

\textit{Status: Overview.  No new claims are made in this section; it
collects and depicts the structure of Part~IV schematically.}

\paragraph{Overall picture.}
Part~IV operates as a closure/consistency layer above the forward
programme of Parts~I--III (\S\ref{sec:reverse_methodology}).
Starting from the obstruction theorems already present in the colour
consistency analysis (\S\ref{sec:colour_completion}), it formalises
the minimal reverse-engineered postulate P7 (rank-3 complex internal
module with Hermitian form and fixed complex volume form), derives
the minimal admissible colour EFT under P7
(\S\ref{sec:min_colour_eft}), and restates the anomaly-cancellation
layer in the presence of the completion
(\S\ref{sec:anomaly_constraints}).
The coverage table (\S\ref{sec:su3_closure_table}) reclassifies the
SU(3)-dependent questions of Parts~I--III against the four status
labels \emph{Closed structurally}, \emph{Sharpened}, \emph{Reframed},
\emph{Still open}.
Proton stability (\S\ref{sec:proton_stability}) then lives in its
proper architectural layer, and the topological sector
(\S\ref{sec:topological_strong_cp}) is honestly recorded as
\emph{sharpening rather than solving} the strong CP problem.
Section~\ref{sec:part4_status} collects closures, open items, and
directional remarks in tabular form
(Tables~\ref{tab:part4_closures}, \ref{tab:part4_open},
\ref{tab:part4_directional}).

\paragraph{Final statement for Part~IV.}
Part~IV converts a pre-existing colour-completion consistency block
and a pre-existing proton-stability discussion into a coherent
reverse-analysis chapter with a formalised postulate~P7, a derived
admissible EFT class, an anomaly-consistency layer, a coverage
bookkeeping of SU(3)-dependent questions, a tabular ledger of
closures, open items, and directional remarks, and a synthesis
figure.
Its results are Level~B within reverse analysis, with two Level~A
obstruction statements internal to ECT, and one Level~C classificatory
formula.
The strong-sector quantitative observables remain inherited from
standard Yang--Mills and QCD phenomenology, constrained by P7 but
not independently derived.
Part~IV neither derives nor closes the remaining strong-sector open
problems; it sharpens what they are and reclassifies what changes
under the exact-colour completion layer.

\part{Summary, Comparisons, and Outlook}
\label{part:summary}
%==============================================================

\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

This section provides a consolidated discussion of the ECT framework:
its conceptual logic, derivational architecture, current achievements,
comparison with neighbouring programmes, observational reach,
limitations, and future directions.

%--------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Conceptual interpretation and scope of the framework}
\label{subsec:conceptual_interp}

ECT proposes that Lorentzian spacetime, quantum dynamics, and
gravitational interactions can all be obtained from a single
underlying structure: a scalar condensate in four-dimensional
Euclidean space with spontaneously broken $O(4)$ symmetry.
This is a working hypothesis supported by the results presented
here at varying levels of rigour, as classified in
Table~\ref{tab:ect-levels}.

This perspective inverts the conventional logic of quantum gravity.
Rather than attempting to quantise an existing spacetime geometry, ECT
starts from a fundamentally Euclidean arena where no distinction
between space and time exists, and recovers the Lorentzian structure
as a candidate effective property of the supplied ordered vacuum.  The
displayed scalar action gives a Lorentzian principal tensor; a physical
metric, clocks/rods and universal sector cone do not follow directly.
The thermodynamic arrow of time is addressed at the level of the
ordered-branch open-system description with clearly stated closure
assumptions~(Section~\ref{sec:second_law_basics}).
The same-medium hypothesis provides a common research framework for
$G_N$, the EFT action scale later matched to $\hbar$, and the scalar
speed map.  Their microscopic ownership and mutual relations are not
derived.

This framework should not be interpreted as claiming that time is
``unreal''.  It proposes that the distinction between temporal and spatial
directions may be a collective property of the ordered vacuum.  The present
result establishes only the conditional scalar principal-symbol
classification; a physical clock and universal metric remain to be derived.

The comparison with closely related Euclidean-to-Lorentzian
constructions~\cite{GirelliLiberatiSindoni2009,MukohyamaUzan2013}
is useful in a second respect as well. It shows that the
basic idea of obtaining Lorentzian characteristic operators from Euclidean
field theory is not unique to ECT, but it also makes clearer which parts of
ECT remain distinctive claims rather than generic consequences of that
shared idea: the spontaneous-symmetry-breaking origin of the preferred
direction, the proposed gravitational completion, and the extension to
quantum and phenomenological sectors.

%--------------------------------------------------------------
\subsection{Derivational architecture: from the $\Phi$-medium to
observable physics}
\label{sec:derivation_architecture}

The status architecture of ECT can be summarised as a directed graph
from the foundational $\Phi$-medium to derived supplied-model results,
conditional reconstructions and Open completion targets
(Figure~\ref{fig:ect_derivation_map}).  The graph is status-separated; it is
not a claim that every major physical sector has emerged from P1--P6.

\paragraph{Step~1: the $\Phi$-medium and the foundational postulates.}
The starting point is a scalar condensate field~$\Phi$ living on a
four-dimensional Euclidean manifold $(M^4,\delta_{AB})$ with an
$O(4)$-invariant action $S_E[\Phi]$.
No external time coordinate is postulated; the theory is fully
relational~(P1--P6).

\paragraph{Step~2: supplied ordered branch.}
Postulate P4 supplies a gradient condensate
$\langle\partial_A\Phi\rangle\neq 0$ selecting a
preferred direction $n_A=\delta_{Aw}$, breaking $O(4)\to O(3)$.
Its dynamical formation from P1--P3 and the descent of physical
macroscopic/quantum sectors remain Open.

\paragraph{Step~3: conditional scalar Lorentzian classification.}
Perturbations around the ordered background experience the effective
ordered-branch kinetic tensor
$K^{AB}=\beta\,\delta^{AB}-\alpha\,n^A n^B$.
For a homogeneous ordered background $n^A=\delta^A_w$, the scalar
principal tensor is Lorentzian when $\alpha>\beta$, with
$K^{AB}=\mathrm{diag}(\beta,\beta,\beta,\beta-\alpha)$ and
$\hat c_*^2=\beta/(\alpha-\beta)$.
This yields a scalar common-length tensor proportional to
$\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ at $\hat c_*=1$; it is not yet a physical
light cone.

\paragraph{Step~4: macroscopic tensor branch (Part~II).}
The macroscopic sector develops as follows:
\begin{itemize}[noitemsep,topsep=2pt]
\item \emph{General relativity.} A separately supplied healthy
  Fierz--Pauli seed could self-couple to an Einstein--Hilbert closure
  under the standard assumptions.  The displayed director map has no
  nonzero TT seed or static-density vertex, so this is a completion
  target rather than a result of the scalar action.
  The scalar--tensor ansatz yields the corrected scalar metric and
  field equations.  A preferred-direction curvature operator resembling an
  Einstein--aether term is a proposed separate extension
  \cite{Jacobson2004}; it is not derived from the displayed scalar-only action
  and remains Open pending a covariant $n^A$ sector and projection audit.
\item \emph{Fundamental constants.}
  $G_N=c_{\rm char}^4/(8\pi M_G^2)$ is a conditional physical-tensor
  matching, while $c_{\rm char}=c_{\rm u}\hat c_*/\mathcal N_\Phi$
  requires a clock map.  Neither is determined by the condensate
  amplitude alone; the phenomenological match
  $\phi_0\approx\bar{M}_{\rm Pl}$~(Ph1, Ph2).
\item \emph{Scale inventory.}
  The energy/matching scales $\phi_0\sim\bar M_{\rm Pl}$ and
  $v_2\approx246$~GeV have distinct declared status.  The kpc quantity
  $L_{\rm gal}$ is a matching length used in Level-C HRC diagnostics, not a third
  field scale; its ECT origin is Open (Section~\ref{sec:three_scales}).
\item \emph{Cosmology.} The ordered branch supplies conditional
  background and perturbation constructions, not a completed numerical
  cosmology.  The fixed orientation determinant does not derive
  vacuum-offset decoupling.  A separately supplied trace-free completion is
  classically shift covariant through $V+C_I$, while a distinct ordinary
  two-slope completion gives a regular late-de-Sitter proof of class but is
  not additive-shift invariant.  Their descent from the $\Phi$ medium, the
  physical matter/photon metric, global state and likelihood remain Open.
  The primordial spectrum~$(n_s,A_s,r)$ is likewise an open target.
\item \emph{Galactic dynamics.} HRC-0 and HRC-3 are the active
  augmented-model response candidates; the slope~4 is conditional algebra
  after a separate static gravity bridge.  Existing SPARC/RAR/BTFR outputs are
  HRC-only algebraic diagnostics.  P1--P6 ownership, source/metric map, and the
  matched $a_{M0}=cH_0/(2\pi)$ coefficient remain Open as stated.
\item \emph{Strong-field sector.} A critical-shell ansatz supplies only
  the conditional Tolman crossover $\rho_*=\hbar c/(2\pi k_BT_*)$ and a
  candidate route to black-hole thermodynamics~(Level~C/Open).  No
  physical $T_*$ or universal shell thickness is derived.  Only the generic
  reduced-state identity is Level~A mathematics; global interacting
  unitarity, purification and the Page curve remain Open.
\item \emph{Preferred-direction benchmark.}  If the hand-set coupling
  $\beta_5\sim m_f/\phi_0$ and the published observable map are
  supplied, they give sensitivity scales
  $\omega_5\sim10^{-10}$~rad/s and E\"otv\"os parameter
  $\eta\sim10^{-15}$.  These are not ECT predictions.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Step~5: quantum coherent branch (Part~III).}
In parallel, the coherent sector develops:
\begin{itemize}[noitemsep,topsep=2pt]
\item \emph{Action scale~$S_0$.} A supplied fixed-core compact-phase EFT
  defines a candidate action coefficient and winding gives integer labels.
  A nonzero global minimum, cross-sector universality and $S_0=\hbar$ are
  Open~(Level~B/Open).
\item \emph{Schr\"odinger equation.} A supplied linear coherent sector
  admits a conditional envelope reduction and the usual uncertainty theorem
  for supplied operators.  The physical operator/state map, CCR
  normalisation and universal $S_0$ are Open~(Level~B/Open).
\item \emph{Vacuum response.} Supplied scalar/QFT calculations compare
  a Dirichlet Casimir BVP, the standard Unruh/KMS target and
  time-dependent mode mixing.  A common physical ECT response bundle,
  state and coupling are Open; no condensate-sector Casimir ratio is
  predicted.
\item \emph{Decoherence and arrow of time.} The influence-functional
architecture yields environmental open-system closures and provides notation
for candidate record channels.  The Di\'osi--Penrose numbers are imported
benchmarks; an ECT gravitational kernel remains Open.  An entropy-growth theorem and a Crooks relation remain Open ECT
constructions: the former requires a named channel/state/entropy functional
and contractivity conditions, while the latter requires forward/reverse
protocols and local detailed balance.
\item \emph{Born rule.} RP may supply an inner product in verified
  subsectors and Gleason constrains an already supplied additive measure.
  Neither result creates probabilities, selects an outcome, or derives the
  physical measure from P1--P6~(conditional Level~B theorem; ECT ownership
  Open).
\item \emph{Exchange topology and spinors.} The
  $\pi_1(\mathcal{M}_2)=\mathbb{Z}_2$ result from
  $d_{\rm spatial}=3$ is Level~A conditional topology for a supplied
  identical-point configuration space.  The physical particle map,
  spin-statistics hypotheses and Dirac matter action remain Open.
\item \emph{Entanglement.} Non-factorisable correlations follow only
  after a nonfactorising state and channel are supplied; a common ordered
  medium is insufficient~(conditional mathematics / Open ECT).
\item \emph{Area-law entropy programme.} A conditional finite-cell
  counting lemma is exact after a coarse-graining, finite local
  capacity, physical split and area-law state class are supplied.
  ECT ownership of those inputs, a physical black-hole bound and
  holographic reconstruction remain Open
  (Theorem~\ref{thm:area_bound}).
\item \emph{Charge quantisation.} Standard representation theory gives
  $q\in\mathbb{Z}\cdot e_0$ after a compact local $U(1)$ bundle, charge
  unit and matter representation are supplied (Level~A conditional
  mathematics).  ECT ownership of those premises, the unbroken photon and
  the observed Standard-Model charge spectrum remains Open.
\item \emph{Post-transition cosmological branch classification.}
  ECT does not yet derive the full nonequilibrium transition or
  the selection of the expanding branch from first principles,
  and a named supplied completion exhibits a regular expanding,
  early-decelerating, late-accelerating history.  P1--P6 do not select
  that completion or history; thermal, recombination, perturbation and
  CMB closures remain Open~(\S\ref{sec:post_transition}).
\item \emph{PES-R operational programme.} PES-R is a bounded
  Level-B organising taxonomy for dynamical admissibility, finite-time
  retention, and pairwise records.  Visibility and qubit/CHSH numbers are
  declared source-model or toy proxies; they do not derive Born weights,
  measurement outcomes, spectra, or a universal quantum--classical boundary.
  ECT-specific kernels and record operators remain Open.
\end{itemize}

\paragraph{Step~6: gauge and matter sectors.}
BR1 supplies a compact global phase.  A local $U(1)$ bundle, unbroken
photon, charge map and matter representations do not follow from that fact;
the non-Abelian $SU(2)$ completion, $W^\pm/Z$ identification and radial-mode
Higgs map are likewise conditional model-building routes (Level~B/Open).
The colour group $SU(3)$ and the fermion-generation structure remain Open.
A minimal colour completion is proposed in
\S\ref{sec:colour_completion}, and the resulting baryon-number
selection rules are analysed as a proton-stability discriminant in
\S\ref{sec:proton_stability}.

\paragraph{Particle spectrum.}
The condensate architecture organises the particle sector into
different status layers.
At the structural or partially established level this includes:
a physical graviton only as an Open tensor-completion target (the fixed $\delta n_A$ map has no TT/static-density seed);
the photon, $W^\pm/Z$, Higgs and fermions only as targets of supplied
gauge/matter completions; their physical bundle, representation, mass and
observable maps remain Open.
The integrability-reduced orientation sector instead retains one
surviving soft scalar $\chi$.  Its mass, abundance and possible
cosmological or dark-sector role remain Open.  For the primary
$\pi_3(S^3)$ sector, topology supplies integer labels only and the
two-derivative energy $E_2(R)\propto R$ collapses.  Any finite particle and
mass spectrum requires a separately derived stabilising action; a possible
secondary-sector owner remains Open.

\paragraph{Step~7: results, benchmarks, tests, and Open gates.}
The map separates strict results from matched benchmarks and explicitly
declared closures.  In particular, $a_M$ and the gravity bridge remain matched/Open;
the deep-HRC slope~4 is Level~A only inside the supplied functional,
conditional after that bridge, and its data comparison is Level~C.  The
no-halo statement is only a property of the stated diagnostic fit,
and environment/orientation signals remain Open programmes.  None predicts
the absence of particle dark matter or of a laboratory signal.
These are summarised in
Figure~\ref{fig:ect_derivation_map} and Tables~\ref{tab:ect_structure}
and~\ref{tab:ect-levels}.
